info.title: AlterCPA Lite — Filter & Cloaking API
info.description: Two subsystems: /api/filter/* manages and copies campaigns, reads the visit journal and statistics and clears the journal via standard API auth with the scope parameter (GET query string only); errors use the {status:"error", error} envelope with HTTP statuses (400 generic and scope, 401 key, 402 unpaid, 403 access/ban, 404 no-id/bad-id/bad-status of postback, 500 db) and the headers X-API-Status / X-API-Error; /fltr/ is the runtime cloaking endpoint with its own URL-embedded auth and x-www-form-urlencoded-only POST, and always answers HTTP 200. Blacklists themselves are managed by the separate blacklist API.

Scope.name: scope
Scope.description: Access scope. Must be in GET query string even when body is JSON. user (default; any unknown value): own campaigns. gang/team: campaigns of the gang members, key owner must be a gang admin. admin/sys/system/all: all campaigns, requires an admin account. An unusable scope gives error scope.

User.name: user
User.description: POST first, then GET. Gang scope: one member of the own gang (a non-member gives scope). Admin scope: owner filter. set: owner of a newly created campaign (required in gang/admin scope, else user-required).

Gang.name: gang
Gang.description: Admin scope only: gang filter (campaigns of its members). POST first, then GET.

ActingUser.name: uu
ActingUser.description: Act as this user (GET or POST). Requires the key owner to be an admin account.

XApiStatus.description: Result status repeated from the body

XApiError.description: Error code repeated from the body

BadRequest.description: Function-level error (HTTP 400): scope, no-site, no-domain, user-required, limit, no-list, bad-list, bad-ip, bad-size, bad-type, bad-value, failed, no-item, bad-item, bad-from, bad-to, bad-user, bad-gang, bad-site, bad-result, bad-ua32, bad-geo; framework error request.

Unauthorized.description: Error key (API key missing or wrong) or auth.

PaymentRequired.description: Error unpaid (active subscription required when paid subscriptions are enabled).

Forbidden.description: Error ban (user banned or inactive) or access (filter/clear under scope=gang).

NotFound.description: postback only: no-id (uid missing), bad-id (campaign not found or not owned), bad-status (status not in any group).

ServerError.description: Error db (database write failed); framework errors func/app.

error.description: Error code. Framework: request, key, auth, unpaid, access, ban, bot, func, app, db. Functions: scope, no-site, no-domain, user-required, limit, no-list, bad-list, bad-ip, bad-size, bad-type, bad-value, failed, no-item, bad-item, bad-from, bad-to, bad-user, bad-gang, bad-site, bad-result, bad-ua32, bad-geo, no-id, bad-id, bad-status

result.description: Reason code: 0=target shown, 1=junk path, 2=wrong device/OS/browser, 3=geo, 4=IPv4 blacklisted, 5=IPv4 net, 6=IPv6, 7=header rule/no UA, 8=bot/preview, 9=protocol, 10=language, 11=trash, 12=URL, 13=no ad click-id, 14=outside schedule

list.description: Blacklist that caused the block; 0 when none

geo.description: Country code, lower case; zz when unknown

ua.description: Raw User-Agent; empty once the raw row is purged

ips.description: IP addresses found in the request headers; [] when none or purged

headers.description: Captured request headers {header name: value}; names as in the blacklist API header IDs, numeric key when unnamed; User-Agent not included. Empty value is the JSON array [].

id.description: item=date: day as YYYYMMDD; item=site: campaign ID

name.description: item=date: YYYY-MM-DD; item=site: campaign domain, or "ID <id>" when the campaign is gone or outside the scope

user.description: item=site only: campaign owner (0 when the campaign was not found)

click.description: All logged visits of the item in the range

white.description: Visits with a non-zero reason (click - black)

reason.description: Visit count per reason code; keys 1..14 always present, zero-filled

reason_pct.description: Same keys: count / click * 100, one decimal

api.description: Cloaking URL: https://{host}/fltr/{owner}-{owner key}-{id}. Contains the campaign owner's API key.

trash.description: First N visits forced to white

wl.description: IP whitelist, one entry (address or a.b.c.d/N network) per line

log.description: Visit-journal mode: 0=log all visits, 1=only target visits, 2=only dummy visits, 3=do not log

tz.description: Schedule time zone (IANA name); empty = server time

get.description: Returns the filter campaigns of the scope: own in user scope, gang members' in gang scope, all (optionally narrowed by user/gang) in admin scope. No pagination, no ordering guarantee. The success body is a bare array (no status envelope).

200.description: Array of campaigns (no envelope); [] when none. Errors are {status,error} objects with HTTP 4xx/5xx (list: scope).

get.description: Returns one campaign of the scope with all editable fields, statistics and postback URL templates. The body is a bare object (no status envelope). Also accepts POST with the same fields. api and postback.* contain the campaign owner's API key. Errors: scope, no-site, no-domain.

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: Campaign ID. Required if domain not provided. When non-zero the lookup is by ID only and domain is ignored.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Campaign name, compared for exact equality with the stored domain (not parsed as a URL); the highest campaign ID wins on duplicates. POST takes priority over GET. Required if uid not provided.

post.description: Creates a new campaign if uid is absent and domain doesn't match an existing one in the scope; the other supplied fields are applied to it in the same call. A new campaign is owned by the scope's user: in gang/admin scope pass user, else user-required; a create is also refused with limit when the owner's plan allows no more campaigns (checked after user-required). Parameters merged from GET+POST (POST wins on collision); only the fields present change. An unknown uid gives no-site.

uid.description: Existing campaign ID. Required for update when not using domain.

domain.description: Campaign name (not parsed as a URL). Required when uid absent. A value different from the stored one renames the campaign.

log.description: Visit-journal mode: 0=log all visits, 1=only target visits, 2=only dummy visits, 3=do not log

wl.description: IP whitelist (multiline: one address or a.b.c.d/N network per line)

uwl.description: URL whitelist (one substring per line; comma = AND)

list.description: Blacklist IDs. IDs outside the campaign owner's global, personal and gang lists are dropped silently; empty clears the selection.

th.description: Schedule window end hour (window active only when an hour or minute is non-zero)

tz.description: Schedule time zone (IANA name); unknown name resets to empty (server time)

200.description: Created or updated campaign reference (also when the call carried no editable fields).

api.description: Cloaking URL for this campaign (owner's key)

post.description: Deletes the campaign (only inside the scope) and purges its visit-journal records.

domain.description: Campaign name (alternative to uid; highest ID wins on duplicates)

200.description: Deleted campaign ID. Errors: scope, no-site, no-domain (HTTP 400), db (HTTP 500).

get.description: Streams a PHP file that POSTs $_SERVER to /fltr/ and dispatches visitors. The campaign owner's API key is embedded in plaintext in the downloaded file, also when a gang admin or an admin downloads it. The body is the file whatever format suffix was requested.

post.description: Adds an IPv4 address, IPv4 network, IPv6 network, or header rule to an existing blacklist the caller may modify. The list kind is determined by the list itself (its type), not by a parameter. Allowed lists: user scope - the key owner's personal lists (system and gang lists refused); gang scope - the gang's lists and the personal lists of the member given in user; admin scope - any list (with user and/or gang the list owner must match). List status and locked (feed/mirror) lists are not checked. Create and manage lists with the blacklist API.

list.description: Target blacklist ID (must be permitted in the scope, else bad-list)

ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address (for list types 1/2/3). Must be public.

size.description: Network mask. IPv4: 8–31. IPv6: 32–128. Required for types 2/3.

value.description: Header value or regular expression (list type 4): non-empty, valid UTF-8, at most 250 characters

regexp.description: Treat value as regular expression (type 4 only)

white.description: Type 4 only: header white-list rule - the visit is blocked when the header does not match or is not sent

type.description: Header ID (type 4 only); unknown IDs are accepted but never match

200.description: Added item details. Errors (HTTP 400): scope, no-list, bad-list, bad-ip, bad-size, bad-type, bad-value, failed (the item could not be stored, e.g. duplicate item).

ip.description: Added IP (string for type 1/3, integer network start for type 2)

get.description: Increments campaign counters. Use the URL templates from filter/get response. No lead row is created and there is no deduplication. Works on the authenticated user's own campaigns only (or the uu user's); scope has no effect. Errors are HTTP 404: no-id, bad-id, bad-status.

parameters.name: payout
parameters.description: Earnings delta for approve group. Positive adds, negative subtracts.

get.description: One page of the visit journal, newest first: one row per checked visit with reason code, matched blacklist, geo, IP, device data, raw User-Agent, discovered IP list and captured request headers. Read-only. Visits are restricted by the campaign owner according to the scope. A visit appears only after the background job condensed it; visits of paused/disabled campaigns and visits skipped by the campaign log mode are never present. Raw fields (ua, ips, headers) are purged earlier (30 days by default) than the rows (90 days), so old rows can come back with empty ua/ips/headers. Fields may also be sent as form data (POST wins).

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: Rows per page; below 1 or non-numeric gives 50, above 1000 is cut to 1000

parameters.name: site
parameters.description: Only visits of this campaign (the ownership condition of the scope still applies)

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Only visits blocked by this blacklist

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: -2 = target shown (reason 0), -1 = any block (reason not 0), any other number = exactly that reason code. Non-numeric is ignored.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: Visitor IP; matched through a 32-bit hash (IPv4 exact, IPv6 hash; different addresses can collide). An invalid IP is ignored.

parameters.name: ua32
parameters.description: crc32 of the User-Agent, as returned in ua32; 0 is ignored

200.description: Journal page. data is an object keyed by row ID in descending order; an empty page is the JSON array []. A page beyond the last returns empty data with the same nav.

get.summary: Visit statistics by date or campaign
get.description: Aggregates the visit journal by day or by campaign over a date range: total, target (black) and dummy (white) visits and a per-reason breakdown with percentages. Read-only. Counts come from the journal, so they differ from the campaign counters of list/get (the journal honours the campaign log mode, omits visits of paused/disabled campaigns, includes checks made by a flow bound to the campaign, and is cut by retention - 90 days by default). Days, from, to and today are computed in the calling user's own time zone (tz of the profile) when the install's per-user time zones setting is on, the stored zone is a valid IANA name and the database server knows it; otherwise in the install's time zone. dataset.tz names the zone used. Errors (HTTP 400): scope, no-item, bad-item, bad-from, bad-to.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Grouping: date = one row per calendar day, site = one row per campaign. Empty gives no-item, other values bad-item.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD (a real calendar date, else bad-from), in the time zone of dataset.tz. After 'to' it is set to 'to'. Default: 'to' minus 6 days.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD (else bad-to), in the time zone of dataset.tz. Empty or in the future gives today.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number over the aggregated rows

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: Rows per page; below 1 gives 50, above 1000 is cut to 1000

200.description: Statistics page. data is keyed by id: item=date newest day first, item=site by campaign name ascending; days/campaigns without visits are absent; a page beyond the end gives data = []. dataset.results maps reason codes 0..14 to labels in the authenticated user's language.

tz.description: IANA name of the time zone the days, from, to and today are in: the calling user's zone when per-user zones are on and usable, otherwise the install's zone

results.1: Request to invalid path or domain

post.description: Deletes the visit-journal rows that filter/log lists for the same six filters (site, list, result, ip, ua32, geo), so a client clears exactly what it can read; no filter at all clears the whole scope. Only the journal rows are deleted: campaign counters of list/get are not changed, and a cleared visit does not come back. A filter that is sent must be read exactly as sent, else the call is refused with bad-site, bad-list, bad-result, bad-ip, bad-ua32 or bad-geo and nothing is deleted; an empty value counts as not sent, 0 of site/list/ua32 means no filter, an array value is refused. Scopes: user clears the caller's visits; gang is never clearable (access for a team admin, scope for any other user); admin alone clears every visit of the install, with user and/or gang only that user's / the team members' visits (a non-numeric user or gang gives bad-user / bad-gang). Order of checks: scope, access, bad-user/bad-gang, the filters, then the delete (db).

site.description: Only visits of this campaign (ownership of the scope still applies). Digits only, else bad-site; 0 or empty = no filter.

list.description: Only visits blocked by this blacklist. Digits only, else bad-list; 0 or empty = no filter.

result.description: -2 = target shown (reason 0), -1 = any block (reason not 0), any other integer = exactly that reason code. Not an integer gives bad-result.

ip.description: Visitor IP, matched through a 32-bit hash (IPv4 exact, IPv6 hash; a colliding address is deleted too). Not an IP gives bad-ip; empty = no filter.

ua32.description: crc32 of the User-Agent. Digits only, else bad-ua32; 0 or empty = no filter.

geo.description: Two-letter country code, case-insensitive. Else bad-geo; empty = no filter.

200.description: Number of journal rows deleted (0 when nothing matched).

post.description: Makes a new campaign from an existing one: the source's settings under a new name, counters at zero. GET with the same parameters in the query string is accepted too. Unlike set, it always creates a new campaign and never updates an existing campaign, so an already used name is allowed (keep the returned id). The copy belongs to the source's owner in every scope and that owner's plan is counted for limit; there is no user-required. All settings are copied, the schedule (wd1..wd7, fh, fm, th, tm, tz) and the visit-journal mode log included; trash is copied as the source's current value; the six counters start at zero; the visits of the source stay with the source. The success body is {status, data} where data is the new campaign exactly as filter/get returns it. Checks in order: scope, no-site, no-domain, limit, db.

uid.description: Source campaign ID, found in the scope. Missing, 0, unknown and foreign all give no-site.

domain.description: Name of the copy: plain text, tags stripped, never parsed as a URL. Missing or empty gives no-domain.

200.description: The new campaign in the envelope. Errors: scope, no-site, no-domain, limit (HTTP 400), db (HTTP 500).

post.description: **Authentication is embedded in the URL path** as `{user_id}-{api_key}-{campaign_id}`. This endpoint is completely separate from the /api/ family: different routing, different auth, no standard framework errors, always HTTP 200 (errors in the body). Request body MUST be x-www-form-urlencoded (POST of $_SERVER). JSON body is not supported. No format suffix; /clo/{token} is an equivalent alias. The request host is not compared with the campaign domain. Each check writes a visit-journal row unless the campaign log mode suppresses it (paused/disabled campaigns never write one); the white/black counters (stats.white / stats.black) are incremented in every mode.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Format: {user_id}-{api_key}-{campaign_id}. Example: 13-4a3bc9d...-1. API key must not contain dashes.

requestBody.description: All $_SERVER keys as x-www-form-urlencoded. Use http_build_query($_SERVER) in PHP.

X-Action.description: The action value; deny on errors

result.description: Real filter decision before training mode override

action.description: Decision after training mode override — use this to dispatch

type.description: black=show target, white=show dummy. The client script dispatches on this value.

ip.description: Resolved visitor IP; false when none could be resolved

reason.description: Code of the real check (also in training modes; 0 in paused/disabled modes). 0=allowed. 1=junk request path, 2=wrong device/OS/browser, 3=geo blocked, 4=IPv4 blacklisted, 5=IPv4 net blacklisted, 6=IPv6 blacklisted, 7=header rule (black match / white miss) or no UA, 8=bot/preview/no IP, 9=wrong protocol, 10=wrong language, 11=trash/warm-up or probing path, 12=URL blacklisted/whitelist miss, 13=no ad click-id, 14=outside the campaign schedule

error.description: bad-request: malformed URL token; access-denied: banned/wrong key/wrong owner; bad-site: campaign not found; no-data: empty POST body
